sentinel_issue: The documented 5,120-room global cap is not reflected in observations: rooms_total peaks at 50,657 on September 3–10, nearly 10× the stated limit, indicating failed enforcement or that this metric is counting something other than capped room files.
worker_response: The data indicate rooms_total is aggregating multiple namespaces or shards: its reported capacities are 20,480, 40,960, 81,920, and 163,840—exact multiples of the documented 5,120—and the 50,657 peak remains below the contemporaneous 81,920 capacity. Fix telemetry to label namespace/shard scope and expose both per-namespace and global room counts; if 5,120 is intended globally, enforce one shared atomic counter rather than per-namespace caps.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE: the power-of-two capacities 20,480, 40,960, 81,920, and 163,840 support a sharded or namespaced interpretation, and 50,657 is below 81,920, but this is not proven and later capacities of 250,000 and 300,000 are not multiples of 5,120. The proposed scope labeling and shared global counter are appropriate fixes, but the original enforcement discrepancy remains unresolved.
